name: Dorsal lateral geniculate nucleus (dLGN) local GABAergic interneuron
anatomy_mentioned: dorsal lateral geniculate nucleus (dLGN), distributed evenly throughout main relay laminae
morphology_summary: Sparse local-circuit neurons (~5.6% of mouse dLGN neurons by stereology; 10-25% in older estimates); complex, widespread, mature bipolar dendritic arbors that cross eye-specific borders; bifunctional neurites that both receive retinal input and release GABA; dual output via axonal F1 terminals and presynaptic dendritic F2 terminals (dendrodendritic, in triads); single EM-reconstructed cell innervated 256 TC cells
ephys_summary: Active dendrites supporting Na+ and long-lasting Ca2+ spikes (axons Na+ only); high-fidelity backpropagation of APs into dendritic appendages; diverse firing (tonic, periodic bursting, burst+tonic, spike-frequency adaptation, rebound bursts); prominent Ih (HCN3-rich, PIP2-modulated); retain ~8-10 retinal inputs (no pruning); F2 GABA release AP-independent, mGluR5/L-type Ca2+ dependent; depolarized by group I and hyperpolarized by group II mGluR agonists; tonic GABA_A inhibition of relay cells at high firing rates
subtypes_noted: Rodent literature treats as one (at most 1-2) homogeneous class. Leist et al., 2016: two mouse subclasses by cluster analysis - small cells (depolarized RMP, stronger anomalous rectification, faster/higher-frequency APs, rebound bursting, higher Ih density, nNOS-negative) vs large cells (lower Ih, nNOS/Nos1-positive). Sanchez-Vives et al., 1996: ferret interlaminar 'PGN-like' parvalbumin-positive subset (species-specific; excited by TC collaterals, rhythmic rebound LTS 1-4 Hz, responds to serotonin, CCK8S, ACh). Transcriptomic section is LLM-generated/unsourced and suggests one main tectum-derived cluster.
